statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-16237 (PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT can read or modify rows despite auto-updatable view WHERE condition) in 16.16 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16237/ lists 16.16 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/629f54970896a84e80574d4aa17c3909e25bc8af on the REL_16_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-16237, which changes src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c, src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c, src/backend/executor/execMain.c and src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h (plus documentation and regression tests) so that INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE through an automatically updatable view checks the view's WHERE condition against the conflicting row and raises an error when the row is not visible through the view; it is in the REL_16_16 release tag and not in REL_16_15. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the source files this fix changes, and it lists CVE-2026-16237 under its 16.16-r0 secfixes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every published postgresql16 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 16.16-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.16 and contains the error message this fix adds ("conflicting row is not visible through view"), while the earlier builds 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 report 16.13, 16.14 and 16.15 and do not contain it; the existing message "new row violates check option for view" is present in every build. 16.16-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-16237 (PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT can read or modify rows despite an auto-updatable view's WHERE condition, whether or not it is a security_barrier view) affects PostgreSQL 18 before 18.7 and is fixed upstream in 18.7: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16237/ and the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-16237 under its 18.7-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The affected code is in the PostgreSQL server, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres in the postgresql18 package. In each published build for Alpine 3.23 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, that binary reports the PostgreSQL release of the same version. The fix makes the server raise the error "conflicting row is not visible through view" instead of updating such a row; that message is present in the 18.7-r0 server binary and absent from the earlier builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0) on both architectures. 18.7-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix; the earlier published builds are built from earlier PostgreSQL 18 releases and recorded as affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-16237, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on an auto-updatable view letting a user with INSERT and UPDATE privileges on the view read and modify every row of its base table despite the view's WHERE condition, in 17.12. Within major version 17, releases before 17.12 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16237/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-16237. The postgres server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix, and 17.12-0 is the lowest published build that does. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
